score_kind: heuristic visual similarity (not a calibrated probability)
verdict: The render reproduces quadrilateral ABCD with correct vertices, all four edges and all four labels; the only visible difference is that the render's strokes are lighter than the original's.

figure_type.original: quadrilateral ABCD: vertical side AB, horizontal sides AD and BC, diagonal side CD
figure_type.render: quadrilateral ABCD: vertical side AB, horizontal sides AD and BC, diagonal side CD

issues.description: Outline strokes in the render are thinner than in the original; the original edges look roughly twice as heavy at the same scale. Render strokes are too thin.
issues.suggestion: Increase the draw line width from 1.0pt to about 1.3-1.5pt on the \draw command for the quadrilateral. Keep the vertex coordinates unchanged.

checks.note: Bottom edge BC is drawn from B to C, ending at both vertices as in the original.
Diagonal CD runs from C to D and ends at D as in the original.
Top edge AD runs from A to D and ends at D as in the original.
Left edge AB is vertical and joins A and B as in the original.
Label C sits below-right of vertex C, matching the original.
Label B sits below-left of vertex B, matching the original.
Label D sits above vertex D, matching the original.
Label A sits above-left of vertex A, matching the original.

matches: Four vertices A, B, C, D are in the same relative positions as the original.
Edges AB, BC, CD and DA are all present and join the correct vertices.
Edge endpoints meet exactly at the labelled vertices, with no overhangs or stubs.
The diagonal CD keeps its slope and meets the top edge at D.
All four labels are present, correctly spelled and bound to their vertices without collisions.
Figure aspect ratio and overall layout match the original.

topology_decisions.reason: The original bottom stroke runs continuously from B to C.
The original diagonal stroke runs from C up to D.
The original top stroke runs horizontally from A to D.
